outcome: Run shared countdown timers on Home Assistant’s own timer helpers.

views.title: Room controls
views.condition: Tap the tablet, or approach it with Controls on approach switched on; lights, covers and timers appear when configured. With actions in Ramka 0.16.0 or later, one-tap shortcuts to a button, script or scene, such as a gate remote's, sit under the awnings, each behind Home Assistant's confirmation unless it sets confirm: false.
views.layout: Ramka landscape layout: 1024–1280 × 720–800 CSS px; phone/portrait dashboard not claimed.

setup: Choose a prefix (default domosenso) and one to sixteen timers, each with a slug id, a plain label and a length of 1 to 86,400 seconds; the default is one General timer of five minutes. Use ids that no helper in your home already has: the component creates only the helpers it names.
Add it with domosenso add timers@0.1.0, then render and deploy: Home Assistant gets one timer helper per entry, named timer.<prefix>_<id>, with Restore switched on.

To show them on a Ramka (0.15.0 or later), list the helpers in its timers input, for example timer.domosenso_general with the label General. Controls gets a standard timer tile for each, and a small countdown badge sits over every screen of the Ramka; tapping either opens Home Assistant’s own timer dialog.

states.label: Ready
states.headline: A timer waits at its length
states.detail: Each helper has a fixed length from its input, five minutes by default. Nothing counts down until someone starts it.

states.label: Running
states.headline: The same time left on every screen
states.detail: The timer is a standard Home Assistant helper. The Ramka’s tile on Controls and its badge both read it.

states.label: Paused
states.headline: A pause keeps the time left
states.detail: A paused timer holds its remaining time. Restore is on, so Home Assistant brings an active or paused timer back after a restart; one that ended while it was down is not replayed.
